claims.text: Plasma nitriding of Ti-6Al-4V will form a TiN-enriched surface layer.
The TiN-enriched surface layer will be durable.
Plasma nitriding will increase the surface hardness of Ti-6Al-4V.
Plasma nitriding will increase the wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V under ambient dry-sliding conditions.
Plasma nitriding at approximately 500–800°C for sufficient duration will promote nitrogen diffusion into the alloy surface.
The treatment will form a thin surface layer.
The treatment will form a uniform surface layer.
Nitrogen introduced during plasma nitriding diffuses into the titanium substrate.
Diffused nitrogen reacts with titanium to precipitate TiN phases.
The precipitated TiN phases are ultra-hard.
TiN phases act as a wear barrier by reducing material removal during sliding contact.
Plasma nitriding will increase surface hardness by approximately 50% or more relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Plasma nitriding will significantly reduce wear rate relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
The surface-property improvements will also hold under moderately lubricated wear conditions at ambient temperature.
The predicted improvements will hold for alloys of similar composition under moderate mechanical and thermal loads.
High temperatures, corrosive environments, or overly aggressive wear may diminish the improvements produced by plasma nitriding.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires both an approximately 50% or greater hardness increase and reduced wear, but the falsification rule uses an 'and' between failure of the hardness and wear outcomes. As worded, failure of only one required outcome may not falsify the hypothesis.
